- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above peak or align with 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >75, reduce by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes; if <70, increase by 0.5–1% to avoid underestimation.
- Sentiment spikes (≥1.0) correlate with price volatility; model should not forecast linear trends; instead, add ±1–2% buffer around median of recent 7-day range.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model often overfits; use 30d median as anchor, adjust ±0.5% based on sentiment direction.
